about.title: San Jacinto Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product can turn an ordinary day in San Jacinto into a trip to the emergency room — whether it's a malfunctioning tool used near State Street, a faulty vehicle part on Ramona Expressway, or a household appliance that failed without warning. California's strict liability rules mean an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent; showing the product was defective and that it caused harm is often enough. That applies whether the flaw was in the design, the manufacturing process, or missing warnings and instructions. Liability can extend beyond the manufacturer to distributors and retailers who sold the item. If you were hurt by something that broke, malfunctioned, or didn't work as intended anywhere in San Jacinto or Riverside County, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can review what happened and explain your options. There's no obligation, and no fee unless you recover.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, an attorney may be able to build your claim around the defect and the harm it caused, rather than proving the manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially share responsibility for a defective product, which may give you more than one avenue to pursue recovery.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: An independent attorney can advise you early on to keep the product itself, packaging, and any related documentation intact — evidence that's often central to proving a defect claim.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability standard, you generally need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, rather than proving the manufacturer failed to use reasonable care. An attorney can help determine which theory fits your situation best.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, if possible, along with any packaging, manuals, or receipts. This evidence is often critical in product liability cases, and an independent attorney can advise you on how to preserve it properly.

items.question: I was hurt by a product near San Jacinto Avenue — does it matter where the injury happened?
items.answer: The location itself typically isn't the focus in a product liability claim, since the issue is the product's defect rather than the surroundings. That said, details about where and how the injury occurred in San Jacinto can still help an attorney understand the full picture of what happened.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive connects you with an independent attorney free of charge, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
